output.summary: An annual herb native to the Azores and found throughout much of the Mediterranean. Its upright stems bear sparse stinging hairs, coarse-toothed leaves and tail-like male flower spikes near the top. In Sicily, its cooked leaves are eaten as a spinach-like vegetable or in soup.
output.edibilityNote: In Sicily, cooked leaves are eaten as nettle spinach or soup; the plant was also eaten in 19th-century Greece.
